verdict.label: Light review
verdict.summary: You must bring your own OAuth app to connect Xero with Composio, configure granular or broad scopes, and abide by rate limits.

composioFit.summary: Composio does not provide a managed Xero app, so you must create a custom auth config using your own registered Xero OAuth app credentials.
whyOwnApp: Composio does not maintain a managed OAuth app for Xero.
You need custom scopes or your own app branding on consent screens.

phases.name: Register Xero App
steps: Go to the Xero Developer Portal and register as a developer.
Create a new app and obtain your Client ID and Client Secret.
phases.handoff: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret from the Xero Developer Portal.

phases.name: Configure Auth in Composio
steps: Open the Composio dashboard and create a new custom auth config for Xero.
Retrieve the redirect URI from Composio and add it to your Xero app settings.
Paste the Client ID and Client Secret into the Composio dashboard.
phases.handoff: Test the authentication flow using your own Xero account.

artefacts.title: Xero App Registration Details
artefacts.body:
App Name: My AI Agent Integration
Company URL: https://example.com
Redirect URI: <Composio callback URL from your auth config>

artefacts.title: Scope Justification for Granular Scopes
artefacts.body: We request granular accounting scopes (such as accounting.invoices) solely to allow our AI agent users to automate accounting workflows and retrieve invoice summaries upon explicit request.

requirements.label: Privacy Policy and Terms of Use
requirements.when: Required for all developer apps as specified in Xero platform terms.

requirements.label: Terms and Conditions Agreement
requirements.when: Must accept Developer Platform Terms and Conditions.

scopes.purpose: Read and manage invoices within Xero organisations.

redirectRules.rule: Must use the exact redirect URI provided by the Composio dashboard in your Xero app configuration.

blockers.cause: Exceeded concurrent (5), minute (60), or daily (5000) limits per connection.
blockers.fix: Implement exponential backoff using the Retry-After header and batch requests where possible.
blockers.fallback: Optimize API call patterns or distribute load across multiple tenant connections.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 401 Forbidden with header WWW-Authenticate: insufficient_scope
blockers.cause: Calling an endpoint requiring a granular scope that has not been requested or authorized yet.
blockers.fix: Update your authorization link to include the necessary granular scope and prompt the user to re-authenticate.
blockers.fallback: Request broad scopes or update permissions flow.

blockers.cause: Using API Data sourced from the Xero developer platform to train or fine-tune artificial intelligence models, LLMs, or machine learning tools.
blockers.fix: Ensure all API data is used strictly for real-time agent execution and app features, never for model training.
blockers.fallback: Remove any pipeline feeding Xero data into model training sets.

checklist.text: Register as a developer on the Xero Developer Portal and accept terms.
Create a new Xero app to obtain Client ID and Client Secret.
Create a custom auth config in the Composio dashboard for Xero.
Add the Composio redirect URI into your Xero developer app settings.
Connect a test Xero organisation via the Composio link to verify scopes.

uncertainties: Exact review wait times for custom app partner applications are not explicitly documented in public snippets.
Exact scope tier lists for every single granular endpoint require checking the live Scopes documentation page.
